messages.subject: Error Compiling
parts:
Hey everyone,

I have a few lines of code which were working in "nimble" version 0.10.1, Windows.
After an update, 0.10.1 -> 0.12.0, the code no longer works and display an error when compiling the code (image attached). I tried a few different versions of "nimble" and came to the conclusion: any version above 0.10.1 gives me that error.

The model is running a DPMM for clustering, with custom priors for the components.

I included an example, easy to run with a very simplified dataset for the model I'm using. The error occurs on the second compileNimble function.

It is weird that it worked before but now it doesn't. I don't know if it is a bug with these versions of "nimble" or if there is a different way to code it in the newer versions.

Many Thanks,
Pedro

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Error Compiling
parts:
Hi Pedro, thanks very much for this report, including the reproducible example.

In version 0.11.0 we made some changes to improve the efficiency of conjugate sampler calculations. In making that change, I see that we are not correctly handling some preparatory steps for compilation involving the size of an object in the conjugate sampler code. This only affects when one has both a Wishart (or inverse Wishart) node that is being sampled by a conjugate sampler and dynamic indexing (as you do, with your BNP formulation).

This will be easy for us to fix, but we may not put out another release for 2-3 months. I'm hoping to fix this on our development branch in the next week or two, so if you want to use a version of nimble more current than 0.10.1, you would be able to use that once available.

One other note: I see that you are also getting a warning about `safeDeparse`.  This warning relates to some improvements we've tried to make to better handle cases where model code has very long lines of code that can cause some internal problems in nimble's compiler. However, I can't reproduce that warning that you are getting. I would very much like to understand why it is happening. Can you confirm for me what version of nimble you are using when you get the warning and that the warning occurs with the exact code in reprex_error.R that you sent?

-chris

messages.author: dee000045d6ab2bf
messages.subject: Re: Error Compiling
parts:
Hey Chris, 

Thank you for clarifying the error in the later versions of nimble. At the moment, I am fine with using "0.10.1" nimble. I just happen to update by miss clicking a button so... thought I would report it. Thank you for continuously updating nimble.

Regarding "safeDeparse": after poking and prodding my code I discovered what it is. The example I provided above is part of a much bigger model I am running which combined regression and mixture models into the same model. The warning occurs when I run:

config <- configureMCMC(cmodel, monitors = c( [insert variables here] ))

This happens no matter what variables I monitor. Removing parts of the model in the nimbleCode function I discovered the "problem" was a line which specified the regression. A long regression.

y[i] ~ dnorm(beta0 +
                   inprod(beta_disc[1:ndisc], x_disc[i, 1:ndisc]) + # betas for discrete vars
                   inprod(beta_cont[1:ndim], x_cont[i,1:ndim]) + # betas for continuous vars
                   inprod(beta_rcs[1:ndim], x_spline[i, 1:ndim]) + # betas for spline vars
                   beta_int_cont[1] * x_disc[i,1] * x_cont[i,1] + beta_int_cont[2] * x_disc[i,1] * x_cont[i,2] + 
                   beta_int_cont[3] * x_disc[i,1] * x_cont[i,3] + beta_int_cont[4] * x_disc[i,1] * x_cont[i,4] +
                   beta_int_cont[5] * x_disc[i,1] * x_cont[i,5] + beta_int_spline[1] * x_disc[i,1] * x_spline[i,1] +
                   beta_int_spline[2] * x_disc[i,1] * x_spline[i,2] + beta_int_spline[3] * x_disc[i,1] * x_spline[i,3] +
                   beta_int_spline[4] * x_disc[i,1] * x_spline[i,4] + beta_int_spline[5] * x_disc[i,1] * x_spline[i,5] , sd = sigma)
  
ndisc = 7, ndim = 6

A response which follows a Normal Distribution of mean (many many variables and interactions) and variance sigma. This causes that warning.

Maybe there is some optimisation I can do, but the model has 30 or so covariates.

The error encountered in the image I attached (from the original post) was discovered in this model, hence why it had that warning message. This does not occur in the reprex_error.R .

Anything else I can provide just say,  but the warning does seem to come up at the right time (if the time is very long expressions). I just wasn't sure what it was initially.

Kind Regards,
Pedro

It looks like the checking we put in is being overly aggressive about emitting a warning message in this case of having a long line in your code. We'll fix that, but in this case there is nothing wrong with what you are doing, and you can ignore the warning.

-chris
